boundary_evidence: PARTIAL RUN, 48 of 81. tools/tu_map.py calls 0x0211cbd0..0x021207a8 one contiguous linker run of 81 function(s) (build/tu_map.json). This TU licenses 0x0211cbd0..0x0211e72c, 48 function(s), ROM ordinals 0..47. Of the other 33, 32 keep their own shards and their own delinks.txt entries; the 33rd is the sourceless hole in EDGE 1 below, which has neither. NOTE the promotion queue's shard_count of 80 counts SOURCE FILES, not members: the run holds 81 functions and one of them has no file.

EDGE 1 -- a sourceless hole splits the run, and it is the only edge. ROM ordinal 48, func_ov006_0211e72c (0x0211e72c, size 0xac), has no source anywhere in the tree: it carries a symbols.txt row but NO src/ file and NO entry in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/delinks.txt at all (the blocks jump from 0x0211e658-0x0211e72c straight to 0x0211e7d8), so the cartridge's own bytes cover that range. It is a banked near-miss whose floor is 26 divergences, reconfirmed independently by glm-5.2, claude-fable-5, grok-4.5 and grok-4.6 in config/match_attempts.jsonl. It sits in the MIDDLE of the run, and no delink block and no TU manifest in this tree expresses a .text claim with a hole in it, so the run can only be licensed as one of its two contiguous sides. This TU is the larger side by member count: 48 below the hole against 32 above it. (The upper side is larger in BYTES -- 0x1fd0 against 0x1b5c -- but it also contains the run's one unmatched member that does have a source, _ZN13dScMgTeresa_c13OnYoshiTryEatEi at 0x02120248, which would split it again into 28 + 3.)

EDGE 2 DOES NOT EXIST, BUT NOT BECAUSE THE PRAGMAS ARE INERT -- they move real bytes and are dissolved by defer_codegen off. Three of the run's seven pragma-carrying legacy files fall inside this range: func_ov006_0211d924 and func_ov006_0211db7c carry opt_common_subs off, and func_ov006_0211e220 carries opt_strength_reduction off. The delete-outright control that notes/agents/roles/writer.md requires was run FIRST and REFUTED the guess that they are belt-and-braces: with all three deleted from this file and nothing else changed, verify drops from 48/48 to 45/48 and the three DIFFs are exactly the three pragma-carrying members (105, 999 and 999 words). So each of the three is load-bearing. A second control separates the two halves of the lever: keeping the push/pop brackets but deleting only #pragma defer_codegen off, with the source order unchanged, ALSO gives 45/48 with the same three DIFFs, and on top of that inverts the emission order to '47 ordinal pair(s) NOT in ROM order'. The brackets therefore bind only while codegen is generated at parse time, and that one pragma buys the bytes and the ROM-ascending order together -- writer.md's settled result from ov006/dScMgHanachan_c, reconfirmed here on the opt_common_subs and opt_strength_reduction families.

DESTRUCTOR ORDER IS REPRODUCIBLE, AND THE RULE THAT SAYS OTHERWISE IS CONDITIONAL. The cartridge orders this class D1 (0x0211cbd0) BELOW D0 (0x0211cbf4). The received rule (writer.md, 'the dtor lever set is closed') is that inline-in-class gives D1-then-D0 and out-of-line gives D2/D0/D1, which would have cost this TU its destructor pair -- because an INLINE destructor cannot be used here at all: with it the key function becomes InitResources at 0x021203fc, which lies above the hole, so this TU would emit no vtable, nothing would odr-use the inline destructor, and neither D1 nor D0 would be emitted (measured on a probe TU that includes an inline-destructor header: one section, no destructor). Measured both ways on the real header with the pinned 2004/b56: out-of-line + deferred codegen emits sections D2, D0, D1; out-of-line + defer_codegen off emits D1, D0, D2. That pragma is therefore a destructor-order lever as well as a pragma-binding and emission-order lever, and include/dScMgTeresa_c.h needs NO edit -- its existing out-of-line declaration is what both this TU and the still-enrolled shards above the hole want.

The class's own vtable, emitted because this TU owns the key function. Extent corroborated three ways, per notes/agents/roles/writer.md: (a) the relocated run in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/relocs.txt is unbroken from 0x0213fa08 (the typeinfo word of the 8-byte offset-to-top/typeinfo preamble) through 0x0213fa98, with the first gap at 0x0213fa9c and the next relocation at 0x0213faa0 belonging to the 8-stride pointer-to-member table that follows; (b) tools/rtti_vtables.py --own dScMgTeresa_c reports 36 slots; (c) the next symbols.txt row after the address point is data_ov006_0213fa9c at 0x0213fa9c. All three give symbol extent 0x0213fa0c..0x0213fa9c = 0x90 = 36 slots, and STORAGE 0x0213fa04..0x0213fa9c = 0x98, which is exactly the size of the .data section this TU emits for it. (The naive next-symbol read happens to be RIGHT here: this table's phantom interior symbol, data_ov006_0213fa0c, sits ON the address point rather than inside the table.) The cartridge keeps its canonical copy at ov006:0x0213fa0c, outside this TU's only licensed range (.text 0x0211cbd0-0x0211e72c), so dsd delinks it from the cartridge independently and discarding this object's copy cannot cost the image a byte.

Homeless. mwcc emits three destructor variants from the one out-of-line definition -- D1, D0, D2 in that order under defer_codegen off -- but the cartridge carries only D1 (0x0211cbd0) and D0 (0x0211cbf4); no address anywhere in config/ names a D2 for this class and no instruction in the image calls one. It has no ROM home, so plain deadstrip rather than deadstrip-duplicate, and production isolation discards it. It is emitted AFTER D0 and before ordinal 2, so it does not disturb the licensed run's ROM-ascending emission order.

notes: Hand-assembled: tools/tubuild.py create ov006/dScMgTeresa_c CANNOT run on this TU. cmd_create handles a sourceless member when it assembles the SOURCE (it writes a banner and warns SOURCELESS), but build_manifest_entry (tubuild.py:959) still calls SP.path_for(name).relative_to(REPO) unguarded, so the run writes src_tu/actors/dScMgTeresa_c.cpp and then dies with "AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'relative_to'" before any manifest entry is written. The generated source was used as a parts list and this manifest was written by hand.

Three legacy files each spelled their own view of the object 'struct C' and the three disagree offset-for-offset (+0x4be0/+0x4be1, +0x4bba/+0x4bbc, and a 0x24-stride row walk). They are renamed apart as TeresaPmfA, TeresaPmfB and RowArray rather than merged; 'struct Elem' had the same collision between func_ov006_0211dad0 and func_ov006_0211e118 and is split into SlotElem and HudElem. tubuild's conflict detector raised all four on the generated source.

decl_common.h is included and matched. It already declares nine of this TU's own members -- func_ov006_0211cca8, 0211d75c, 0211d7b4, 0211d7ec, 0211dd6c, 0211ddcc, 0211e118, 0211e29c, 0211e460 -- seven of them as void* where the legacy file used char*, unsigned char* or a shadow struct. Those seven definitions are spelled to match the header and take a one-line cast alias in the body, per writer.md's fix pattern; the two already-char* ones are unchanged. decl_common.h also types func_ov004_020af948 as (void*, int, int, void*) where the legacy file said (int, int, int, int), so func_ov006_0211ddcc's call site carries two casts.
